title: Enforce scalar/array type conformance in the check_schema walker (closes #171)
objective: Close #171 (GOV-0071): the check_schema JSON-schema-lite walker enforced required / enum / pattern / additionalProperties and the object-must-be-a-mapping rule, but did NOT refuse a value whose JSON type mismatched a declared scalar/array `type` -- an `array` given an object was silently skipped, and string/number/integer/boolean were never type-checked. Add deterministic type conformance for array/string/integer/number/boolean at any depth (integer/number exclude Python bool, which is an int subclass). This closes the gap for all ~25 gate-validated artifacts at once (Option 1 from #171), rather than sprinkling per-field code controls. The typed planning fields the G06 ladder added (execution_budget, stop_conditions, dependencies, ...) become type-enforced at the schema layer.
business_value: The value of the typed schema extensions the G06 ladder shipped depends on the walker actually checking types; until now a malformed type passed the schema layer and was only caught (if at all) by a downstream code control. One small deterministic change hardens every governed artifact's type discipline and removes the need for per-field type code controls.
in_scope: scripts/badf_gate.py: check_schema walker -- add scalar/array type conformance (array/string/integer/number/boolean), integer/number excluding bool
